title: coordinated-haltpoint-controller-for-ab-shadow-drain
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a HaltPointController that coordinates AB experiments with shadow-drain safety gates and automatic rollback triggers. Backwards-compatible; requires CRD install and a short console feature flag rollout.
description:
Summary: Introduces a HaltPointController that provides explicit halt points in staged rollouts (canaries, A/B lanes, and shadow captures). The controller coordinates traffic draining for shadow lanes and enforces safety gates before promoting variants. Motivation: Several incidents (see SUP-4421) showed that implicit shadow drains combined with delayed telemetry can cause stale sessions and spurious successes—this PR implements explicit checkpoints and an automated rollback advisor to reduce blast radius and make promotes deterministic.

What this PR does: - CRD: haltpoint.redwood.ai/v1 (HaltPoint) to declare checkpoints, metrics anchors, and drain windows. - Controller: src/controller/haltpoint_controller.go implements reconcile loop, cohort-aware session fencing, and a traffic-drain state machine (Active -> Draining -> Quarantine -> Promoted/Aborted). - Traffic integration: pkg/rollout/traffic_splitter.go extended with a DrainHint protocol used by the routing layer to steer shadow and canary traffic during halt windows. - Safety gates: configurable SLO gates (latency percentile, error-rate, and quality regression) and a TTL-based quarantine where traffic is forced back to stable if metrics stop reporting. - Rollback advisor: a heuristic engine that scores signal divergence and recommends an automatic abort when score exceeds threshold; outputs annotated events to audit log for human review. - Tests: integrated canary simulation harness (tests/integration/haltpoint_sim_test.go) plus unit coverage for session fencing and drain transitions. - Console: adds a HaltPoint panel to the Rollouts UI (console/ui/rollouts/haltpoint-panel.tsx) that exposes live state, metric anchors, and a one-click abort/pause action.

Backwards compatibility & rollout plan: The controller is fully additive. To enable, operators must apply the CRD and a short feature-flag flip in Console (controlled rollout across accounts). We plan a staged rollout: internal canaries -> a small set of customer accounts -> global. Follow-up (small) PR will add RBAC scopes to Dedicated manifests.

Checklist: - [x] CRD schema and validation - [x] Controller reconcile and unit tests - [x] Integration simulation harness - [x] Console UI panel + telemetry endpoints - [x] Documentation: docs/operations/haltpoint-playbook.md - [x] Runbook and playbook linked to SU P-4421

Operational notes: The HaltPoint CRD allows short-circuiting promotes in case of missing telemetry (safety TTL). DrainHint is intentionally lightweight (header + routing annotation) so it can be applied to both hosted and private deployments. The Rollback Advisor emits a detailed event (reason, metrics snapshot, score) to make automated aborts auditable.

Example HaltPoint YAML (CRD usage): `apiVersion: haltpoint.redwood.ai/v1
kind: HaltPoint
metadata:
  name: canary-halt-2026-02
spec:
  targetVariant: v2
  cohortSelector: "region=eu,plan=premium"
  gates:
    latencyP95Ms: 220
    errorRatePct: 0.5
  drainWindowSeconds: 30
  quarantineTTLSeconds: 60
  rollbackScoreThreshold: 0.75`

Why this is different from other rollout controllers: HaltPoint makes the checkpoint first-class: it couples an explicit drain lifecycle with session-fencing semantics and a TTL for missing telemetry rather than silently proceeding. This reduces time-to-detect regressions for low-traffic cohorts and makes automated aborts explainable in audit logs.

Open follow-ups: - RBAC for Dedicated (small manifest change) - Add metric decay model to reduce sensitivity on sparse cohorts - UX: compact timeline widget for multi-haltpoint rollouts
